rows.question: What did the Finance Minister say about capital expenditure?
rows.answer:
### Direct answer
Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said that the government will continue to prioritise capital expenditure to sustain India’s growth momentum while ensuring fiscal discipline. Speaking at HSBC India’s Third Annual Financial Inclusion Gathering in Mumbai, Sitharaman said capital expenditure had delivered good results over the past four to five years through its multiplier effect and would remain an important part of the government’s growth strategy. [S1]
### Detailed explanation
Addressing the balance between welfare commitments and fiscal consolidation, the Finance Minister highlighted the role of government schemes in improving access to basic services, including food security, housing, sanitation, drinking water and healthcare insurance. Sitharaman also identified credit access, insurance and pensions as priorities for the next phase of financial inclusion. She reiterated the government’s goal of achieving insurance coverage for all by 2047 and said credit access was important for people seeking to start or expand businesses. On employment and skills, she said the government wanted every district to have AI training-capable centers to prepare young people for AI-enabled jobs and address the gap between industry requirements and the skills of graduates. [S1]

rows.question: What is ISRO's CMS-03 satellite?
rows.answer:
### Direct answer
The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has successfully launched its next-generation navigation satellite, NVS-03, marking a significant step towards strengthening the country’s indigenous satellite navigation capabilities. [S1]
### Detailed explanation
Speaking to the media, Dr Narayanan said ISRO had placed its third indigenous atomic clock in orbit aboard NVS-03, while two indigenous atomic clocks were already functioning in orbit. He added that the satellite had been launched as part of India’s Regional Navigation Satellite System, which aims to provide navigation services across the country and up to 1,500 kilometres beyond its borders. [S1]
Explaining the programme, the ISRO Chairman said it envisages a constellation of seven satellites in orbit to provide these services. He added that NVS-03 was the fourth satellite launched under the programme and that signals from four satellites could be used for multiple purposes. He said the constellation would need to be completed before navigation services could be integrated with mobile systems for wider public use. [S1]
### Related coverage
- "Vice President and PM Modi Congratulate ISRO and Indian Navy on Successful Launch of CMS-03" (2025-11-02): Vice President C P Radhakrishnan and Prime Minister Narendra Modi have congratulated Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) and Indian Navy on the successful launch of India’s heaviest communication satellite, CMS-03. In a social media post, Vice President Radhakrishnan highlighted how India’s mighty LVM3-M5 rocket roared to the skies once again with the successful launch of GSAT-7R (CMS-03). He pointed out that it is now the heaviest and most advanced communication satellite for the Indian Navy placed into Geosynchronous Transfer Orbit (GTO). [S2]
- "India Launches Heaviest Military Communication Satellite CMS-03 from Sriharikota" (2025-11-02): India’s space agency ISRO successfully launched the LVM3-M5 rocket from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre in Sriharikota today at 5:35 pm. The rocket carried CMS-03, the country’s heaviest communication satellite ever sent to space. It marked the fifth operational flight of the LVM3 launcher. [S4]
